title: Lip balm for dry lips: SPF, tinted or natural, and how to choose
body:
Cold wind, central heating and hot drinks all leave lips dry in winter, and a good lip balm is the simplest fix. But balms are not all the same: some carry an SPF, some add a sheer tint, and some are just a few plant oils, butters and wax. Here is how to choose a lip balm for dry lips, what is inside each type and how to get the most from it.

What a lip balm does

Lips have a very thin outer layer and no oil glands of their own, so they dry out faster than the rest of the face. A balm puts a soft layer of oils, butters and wax over them, which keeps them feeling comfortable for longer. Most balms are built from the same few things: plant oils such as almond, avocado or jojoba; butters such as shea, mango or kokum; and a wax, often beeswax, that holds it all together.

SPF lip balm

Lips burn too, on bright winter days, ski trips and holidays as much as in summer. Vilvah Milk Lip Balm SPF 30 PA+++ (£9.99) uses mineral filters, zinc oxide and titanium dioxide, in a base of coconut oil, shea butter, soy butter, kokum butter and soy milk extract, with a soft vanilla note. Apply it before going outside, and reapply often, especially after eating, drinking or swimming. It works on its own or under lipstick.

Tinted lip balm

A tinted lip balm adds a sheer wash of colour as well as moisture, so it can stand in for a lipstick on busy days.

  • Deyga Beetroot Lip Balm Classic (from £10.99, 10g pot) takes its rosy tint from beetroot extract, in almond, avocado and jojoba oils with shea butter and beeswax. The same balm comes as a twist-up Beetroot Lip Balm Stick (from £13.99, 5.5g) for your pocket.
  • Vilvah Rose Milk Lip Balm (£9.99) gives a soft pink tint, with paneer rose extract, olive squalane, avocado butter, shea butter and vitamin E.
  • Vilvah Mango Shake Lip Balm (£9.99) leaves a reddish-orange tint, with Alphonso mango pulp extract, mango butter, coconut milk and olive squalane.
  • Vilvah Filter Kaapi Lip Balm (£9.99) has a subtle brown tint inspired by South Indian filter coffee, with coffee oil, coffee extract, shea butter, coconut milk and almond oil.
  • Vilvah Grape Fruit Lip Balm (£6.99) has just six ingredients, with a little red iron oxide for a sheer tint and grapefruit essential oil for a zesty scent.

Can't choose? The Vilvah Tinted Lip Balm Kit (£17.99) puts two tinted balms in one box.

Natural lip balm with a short ingredient list

If you prefer a plain balm with nothing extra, look for a short list of oils, butter and wax.

  • Deyga Shea Butter Lip Balm (£9.99, 8g): almond oil, jojoba oil, beeswax, shea butter, vanilla extract and vitamin E, in a vanilla or shea version.
  • Vilvah Natural Lemon Lip Balm (£6.99): organic shea butter, avocado oil, almond oil, unrefined beeswax and lemon essential oil.

For a rich, jar-style lip butter, Highborn London Superior Lip Butter (£22.50, 15ml, or a 50ml jar) is made with organic palm oil certified by the RSPO.

How to use a lip balm

  1. Start with clean, dry lips.
  2. Apply a thin layer with the stick or a clean fingertip, and reapply whenever lips feel dry.
  3. At night, use a thicker layer so it can sit on your lips while you sleep.
  4. Once or twice a week, use a lip scrub first. A balm spreads more evenly on smooth lips; our lip scrub guide explains how.
  5. In the sun, choose an SPF balm and reapply often.

Good to know

  • Try not to lick your lips: saliva dries quickly and leaves them drier than before.
  • Many balms contain beeswax. If you avoid it, check the Ingredients tab on each product before you buy.
  • Patch test balms with essential oils, such as the lemon and grapefruit balms, before first use.
  • Cracked or sore lips that do not settle after a week or two are worth showing to a pharmacist or your GP.
  • Lip balms make easy stocking fillers: see our stocking fillers guide.
